queries.description: Summarizes active transaction count and oldest transaction age using information_schema.INNODB_TRX.

scaling_factor.note: Holds the InnoDB trx_sys mutex while scanning active transactions; scales with active transaction count. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS 'Total Active Transactions', IFNULL(MAX(TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW())), 0) AS 'Oldest Transaction Age (seconds)' FROM information_schema.INNODB_TRX

queries.description: Summarizes active transaction count and oldest transaction age using Performance Schema. Safer alternative.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema transaction events; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS 'Total Active Transactions', IFNULL(MAX(ROUND(t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000, 0)), 0) AS 'Oldest Transaction Age (seconds)' FROM performance_schema.events_transactions_current t JOIN performance_schema.threads th ON t.THREAD_ID = th.THREAD_ID WHERE t.STATE = 'ACTIVE' AND th.PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL

queries.description: Lists all user tables sorted by total size (data + index) with row counts and free space. Useful for capacity planning.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); dynamic metadata (TABLE_ROWS, DATA_LENGTH) cached by information_schema_stats_expiry (default 86400s). Scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA AS `Schema`, TABLE_NAME AS `Table`, ENGINE AS `Engine`, TABLE_ROWS AS `Rows`, ROUND(DATA_LENGTH / 1073741824, 2) AS `Data (GB)`, ROUND(INDEX_LENGTH / 1073741824, 2) AS `Index (GB)`, ROUND((DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) / 1073741824, 2) AS `Total (GB)`, ROUND(DATA_FREE / 1048576, 2) AS `Data Free (MB)` FROM information_schema.tables WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' ORDER BY (DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) DESC

queries.description: Lists all user tables with raw size columns sorted by total size. Simpler variant of top_20_largest_tables.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); dynamic metadata cached by information_schema_stats_expiry. Scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, TABLE_ROWS, DATA_LENGTH, INDEX_LENGTH, DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH AS total_size FROM information_schema.tables WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' ORDER BY total_size DESC

queries.description: Finds tables missing a primary key. Tables without PKs cause replication and performance issues with InnoDB.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES and I_S.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS data dictionary views (MySQL 8.0+); scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT t.TABLE_SCHEMA, t.TABLE_NAME, t.ENGINE, t.TABLE_ROWS FROM information_schema.tables t LEFT JOIN information_schema.table_constraints c ON t.TABLE_SCHEMA = c.TABLE_SCHEMA AND t.TABLE_NAME = c.TABLE_NAME AND c.CONSTRAINT_TYPE = 'PRIMARY KEY' WHERE t.TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND t.TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' AND c.CONSTRAINT_NAME IS NULL ORDER BY t.TABLE_ROWS DESC

queries.description: Identifies tables with significant free space (DATA_FREE), indicating potential fragmentation from deletes or updates.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); dynamic metadata cached by information_schema_stats_expiry. Scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, DATA_LENGTH, DATA_FREE, ROUND(DATA_FREE / DATA_LENGTH * 100, 2) AS fragmentation_pct FROM information_schema.tables WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' AND DATA_LENGTH > 0 AND DATA_FREE > 0 ORDER BY DATA_FREE DESC

queries.description: Finds auto-increment columns that have used more than 50% of their range. Prevents unexpected overflow.

scaling_factor.note: Uses sys.schema_auto_increment_columns which reads I_S.TABLES and I_S.COLUMNS; scales with table count.

queries.name: Auto Increment Usage (>50%)
queries.command: SELECT table_schema AS `Schema`, table_name AS `Table`, column_name AS `Column`, data_type AS Type, ROUND(auto_increment_ratio * 100, 2) AS usage_percentage, max_value, auto_increment AS current_value FROM sys.schema_auto_increment_columns WHERE auto_increment_ratio >= 0.5

queries.description: Lists user tables not using the InnoDB storage engine. Non-InnoDB tables miss out on ACID compliance and crash recovery.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with table count.

queries.name: User Tables Not Using InnoDB
queries.command: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, ENGINE, TABLE_ROWS, DATA_LENGTH FROM information_schema.tables WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' AND ENGINE != 'InnoDB' ORDER BY DATA_LENGTH DESC

queries.description: Finds indexes with zero reads since server start by cross-referencing I_S.STATISTICS with PFS I/O wait stats. Candidates for removal.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.STATISTICS data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+) and PFS table_io_waits_summary; scales with total index count across all schemas.

queries.command: SELECT s.TABLE_SCHEMA, s.TABLE_NAME, s.INDEX_NAME, s.COLUMN_NAME FROM information_schema.statistics s LEFT JOIN performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_index_usage i ON s.TABLE_SCHEMA = i.OBJECT_SCHEMA AND s.TABLE_NAME = i.OBJECT_NAME AND s.INDEX_NAME = i.INDEX_NAME WHERE s.TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND s.INDEX_NAME != 'PRIMARY' AND (i.COUNT_STAR IS NULL OR i.COUNT_STAR = 0) ORDER BY s.TABLE_SCHEMA, s.TABLE_NAME, s.INDEX_NAME

queries.description: Finds indexes that share the same leading column(s), indicating potential redundancy.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.STATISTICS data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with total index count across all schemas.

queries.command: SELECT s1.TABLE_SCHEMA, s1.TABLE_NAME, s1.INDEX_NAME AS index1, s2.INDEX_NAME AS index2, s1.COLUMN_NAME FROM information_schema.statistics s1 JOIN information_schema.statistics s2 ON s1.TABLE_SCHEMA = s2.TABLE_SCHEMA AND s1.TABLE_NAME = s2.TABLE_NAME AND s1.COLUMN_NAME = s2.COLUMN_NAME AND s1.SEQ_IN_INDEX = s2.SEQ_IN_INDEX AND s1.INDEX_NAME < s2.INDEX_NAME WHERE s1.TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY s1.TABLE_SCHEMA, s1.TABLE_NAME

queries.description: Finds foreign key columns that lack a supporting index. Missing indexes on FK columns cause slow joins and cascading operations.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS and I_S.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE data dictionary views (MySQL 8.0+); scales with table and constraint count.

queries.command: SELECT rc.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA, rc.TABLE_NAME, rc.CONSTRAINT_NAME, kcu.COLUMN_NAME FROM information_schema.referential_constraints rc JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage kcu ON rc.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA = kcu.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA AND rc.CONSTRAINT_NAME = kcu.CONSTRAINT_NAME LEFT JOIN information_schema.statistics s ON kcu.TABLE_SCHEMA = s.TABLE_SCHEMA AND kcu.TABLE_NAME = s.TABLE_NAME AND kcu.COLUMN_NAME = s.COLUMN_NAME WHERE rc.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND s.INDEX_NAME IS NULL

queries.description: Finds user accounts with empty passwords (excluding socket auth and locked+expired accounts). MySQL/Aurora variant.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE (authentication_string = '' OR authentication_string IS NULL) AND plugin NOT IN ('auth_socket', 'unix_socket') AND NOT (account_locked = 'Y' AND password_expired = 'Y')

queries.description: Finds user accounts with empty passwords. MariaDB variant using mysql.global_priv for account_locked check.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user and mysql.global_priv system privilege tables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT u.User, u.Host FROM mysql.user u JOIN mysql.global_priv gp ON u.User = gp.User AND u.Host = gp.Host WHERE (u.authentication_string = '' OR u.authentication_string IS NULL) AND u.plugin NOT IN ('auth_socket', 'unix_socket') AND NOT (COALESCE(JSON_VALUE(gp.Priv, '$.account_locked'), 'false') = 'true' AND u.password_expired = 'Y')

queries.description: Finds accounts whose host is exactly '%', meaning the account may connect from any host. Scoped to that one value deliberately: a host carrying a wildcard within a narrower pattern, such as 10.% or %.example.com, restricts where the account may connect from and is not reported.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE Host = '%'

queries.description: Shows SSL/TLS configuration: certificate paths, required transport, TLS versions, and cipher suites.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE variable_name IN ('have_ssl', 'have_openssl', 'ssl_ca', 'ssl_cert', 'ssl_key', 'require_secure_transport', 'tls_version', 'tls_ciphersuites')

queries.description: Shows key connection metrics: connected/running/cached threads, max used connections, and aborted counts.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server status counters; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SHOW GLOBAL STATUS WHERE variable_name IN ('Threads_connected', 'Threads_running', 'Threads_cached', 'Threads_created', 'Max_used_connections', 'Connections', 'Aborted_connects', 'Aborted_clients')

queries.description: Shows current and total connections per user account.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema users summary table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT USER, CURRENT_CONNECTIONS, TOTAL_CONNECTIONS FROM performance_schema.users WHERE USER IS NOT NULL AND USER != 'event_scheduler' ORDER BY CURRENT_CONNECTIONS DESC

queries.description: Finds queries running longer than 60 seconds using Performance Schema threads. Safe, mutex-free alternative to I_S.processlist.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads table; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT PROCESSLIST_ID AS ID, PROCESSLIST_USER AS USER, PROCESSLIST_HOST AS HOST, PROCESSLIST_DB AS DB, PROCESSLIST_COMMAND AS COMMAND, PROCESSLIST_TIME AS TIME, PROCESSLIST_STATE AS STATE, LEFT(PROCESSLIST_INFO, 200) AS query_preview FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_COMMAND NOT IN ('Sleep', 'Daemon') AND PROCESSLIST_COMMAND IS NOT NULL AND PROCESSLIST_TIME > 60 AND PROCESSLIST_USER != 'event_scheduler' ORDER BY PROCESSLIST_TIME DESC

queries.description: Finds queries running longer than 60 seconds using information_schema.processlist. Fallback when PFS is unavailable.

scaling_factor.note: Queries information_schema.processlist which holds the global thread manager mutex; scales with active threads and can cause contention on busy systems. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT ID, USER, HOST, DB, COMMAND, TIME, STATE, LEFT(INFO, 200) AS query_preview FROM information_schema.processlist WHERE COMMAND NOT IN ('Sleep', 'Daemon') AND TIME > 60 AND USER != 'event_scheduler' ORDER BY TIME DESC

queries.description: Finds transactions running longer than 10 minutes using PFS events_transactions_current with current statement details.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema transaction and statement events; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT FORMAT_PICO_TIME(trx.timer_wait) AS transaction_duration, PROCESSLIST_ID AS connection_id, trx.thread_id AS thread_id, trx.event_id AS transaction_event_id, trx.isolation_level AS isolation_level, trx.autocommit AS autocommit, stm.current_schema AS database_name, stm.sql_text AS current_query, stm.rows_examined AS rows_examined, stm.rows_affected AS rows_affected, stm.rows_sent AS rows_sent, IF(stm.end_event_id IS NULL, 'Running', 'Completed') AS statement_state, ROUND(stm.timer_wait/1000000000000, 3) AS statement_time_sec FROM performance_schema.events_transactions_current trx JOIN performance_schema.events_statements_current stm USING (thread_id) JOIN performance_schema.threads USING (thread_id) WHERE trx.state = 'ACTIVE' AND trx.timer_wait > 600000000000000
queries.note: Shows transactions running longer than 10 minutes. Requires events_transactions_current consumer to be enabled in performance_schema.

queries.description: Finds transactions running longer than 10 minutes using information_schema.innodb_trx. Fallback for when PFS is unavailable.

scaling_factor.note: Holds the InnoDB trx_sys mutex while scanning active transactions; scales with active transaction count. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT trx_id AS transaction_id, trx_state AS state, trx_started AS started, TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW()) AS duration_seconds, trx_mysql_thread_id AS connection_id, trx_tables_locked AS tables_locked, trx_rows_locked AS rows_locked, trx_rows_modified AS rows_modified, LEFT(trx_query, 200) AS current_query FROM information_schema.innodb_trx WHERE TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW()) > 600 ORDER BY trx_started

queries.description: Returns the total deadlock count since server start. MariaDB variant using SHOW GLOBAL STATUS.

scaling_factor.note: Reads a server status counter; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'Innodb_deadlocks'

queries.description: Returns the total deadlock count since server restart. For MariaDB, Innodb_deadlocks is a status variable. For Aurora MySQL and MySQL, we read from information_schema.innodb_metrics.

scaling_factor.note: Reads a single row from information_schema.innodb_metrics; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT NAME, COUNT AS deadlock_count FROM information_schema.innodb_metrics WHERE NAME = 'lock_deadlocks'

queries.description: Shows current metadata locks on user schemas. Helps diagnose DDL blocking and lock contention.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema metadata_locks table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_TYPE, OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, LOCK_TYPE, LOCK_DURATION, LOCK_STATUS, OWNER_THREAD_ID FROM performance_schema.metadata_locks WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys')

queries.description: Shows per-table I/O statistics: read/write counts and latencies. Identifies I/O-heavy tables.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema table_io_waits_summary table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, COUNT_READ, COUNT_WRITE, COUNT_FETCH, COUNT_INSERT, COUNT_UPDATE, COUNT_DELETE, SUM_TIMER_READ/1000000000 AS READ_LATENCY_MS, SUM_TIMER_WRITE/1000000000 AS WRITE_LATENCY_MS FROM performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_table WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY SUM_TIMER_WAIT DESC

queries.description: Shows per-file I/O statistics: read/write counts, bytes, and latencies. Identifies I/O bottlenecks at the file level.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema file_summary table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT FILE_NAME, COUNT_READ, COUNT_WRITE, SUM_NUMBER_OF_BYTES_READ, SUM_NUMBER_OF_BYTES_WRITE, SUM_TIMER_READ/1000000000 AS READ_LATENCY_MS, SUM_TIMER_WRITE/1000000000 AS WRITE_LATENCY_MS FROM performance_schema.file_summary_by_instance ORDER BY SUM_TIMER_WAIT DESC

queries.description: Lists tables with the highest read counts. Identifies read-heavy workload targets.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema table_io_waits_summary table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, COUNT_READ, SUM_TIMER_READ/1000000000 AS READ_LATENCY_MS FROM performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_table WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY COUNT_READ DESC

queries.description: Lists tables with the highest write counts. Identifies write-heavy workload targets.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema table_io_waits_summary table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, COUNT_WRITE, SUM_TIMER_WRITE/1000000000 AS WRITE_LATENCY_MS FROM performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_table WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY COUNT_WRITE DESC

queries.description: Lists tables with the highest total I/O latency. Identifies tables causing I/O bottlenecks.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema table_io_waits_summary table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, SUM_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000 AS TOTAL_LATENCY_MS, COUNT_STAR AS TOTAL_OPERATIONS FROM performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_table WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY SUM_TIMER_WAIT DESC

queries.description: Aggregates all schema objects (tables, views, routines, triggers, events) by type per schema.

scaling_factor.note: Uses sys.schema_object_overview which aggregates all schema objects; scales with total object count.

queries.command: SELECT db AS schema_name, object_type, count FROM sys.schema_object_overview ORDER BY db, object_type

queries.description: Lists all user-defined triggers with their event type and timing.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TRIGGERS data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING FROM information_schema.triggers WHERE TRIGGER_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME

queries.description: Lists all scheduled events with their status, type, and last execution time.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.EVENTS data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with event count.

queries.command: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, LAST_EXECUTED FROM information_schema.events WHERE EVENT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema') ORDER BY EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME

queries.description: Lists all stored procedures in user schemas.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.ROUTINES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with routine count.

queries.command: SELECT ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME, ROUTINE_TYPE, CREATED, LAST_ALTERED FROM information_schema.routines WHERE ROUTINE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND ROUTINE_TYPE = 'PROCEDURE' ORDER BY ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME

queries.description: Lists all stored functions in user schemas.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.ROUTINES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with routine count.

queries.command: SELECT ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME, ROUTINE_TYPE, CREATED, LAST_ALTERED FROM information_schema.routines WHERE ROUTINE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND ROUTINE_TYPE = 'FUNCTION' ORDER BY ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME

queries.description: Lists all foreign key constraints with their update and delete rules.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with constraint count.

queries.command: SELECT CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, CONSTRAINT_NAME, UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA, REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME, UPDATE_RULE, DELETE_RULE FROM information_schema.referential_constraints WHERE CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME

queries.description: Lists partitioned tables with partition method, expression, row counts, and partition count.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.PARTITIONS data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with partition count.

queries.command: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, PARTITION_METHOD, PARTITION_EXPRESSION, SUM(TABLE_ROWS) AS TABLE_ROWS, COUNT(PARTITION_NAME) AS PARTITION_COUNT FROM information_schema.partitions WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND PARTITION_NAME IS NOT NULL GROUP BY TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, PARTITION_METHOD, PARTITION_EXPRESSION ORDER BY TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME

queries.description: Lists queries sorted by total execution time from statement digests. Identifies the most time-consuming queries.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT DIGEST_TEXT, COUNT_STAR, SUM_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000 AS TOTAL_TIME_MS, AVG_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000 AS AVG_TIME_MS, SUM_ROWS_EXAMINED, SUM_ROWS_SENT FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE SCHEMA_NAME NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY SUM_TIMER_WAIT DESC

queries.description: Shows min/avg/max latency per query digest. Identifies queries with high variance.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT DIGEST_TEXT, COUNT_STAR, MIN_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000 AS min_ms, AVG_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000 AS avg_ms, MAX_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000 AS max_ms FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE SCHEMA_NAME NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY MAX_TIMER_WAIT DESC

queries.description: Finds queries performing full table scans (no index used or no good index). Candidates for index optimization.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT DIGEST_TEXT, COUNT_STAR, SUM_NO_INDEX_USED, SUM_NO_GOOD_INDEX_USED, SUM_ROWS_EXAMINED FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE SUM_NO_INDEX_USED > 0 OR SUM_NO_GOOD_INDEX_USED > 0 ORDER BY SUM_ROWS_EXAMINED DESC

queries.description: Finds queries creating temporary tables on disk. Indicates queries that may benefit from larger tmp_table_size or query optimization.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT DIGEST_TEXT, COUNT_STAR, SUM_CREATED_TMP_TABLES, SUM_CREATED_TMP_DISK_TABLES FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE SUM_CREATED_TMP_DISK_TABLES > 0 ORDER BY SUM_CREATED_TMP_DISK_TABLES DESC

queries.description: Shows hosts with connection errors from the PFS host_cache. Helps identify network issues or misconfigured clients.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema host_cache table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT IFNULL(HOST,IP) AS HOST, SUM_CONNECT_ERRORS, FIRST_SEEN, LAST_SEEN FROM performance_schema.host_cache WHERE SUM_CONNECT_ERRORS > 0 ORDER BY SUM_CONNECT_ERRORS DESC

queries.description: Aggregates SQL statement errors and warnings per user/host. Identifies problematic application accounts.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_account table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT USER, HOST, SUM(SUM_ERRORS) AS SUM_ERRORS, SUM(SUM_WARNINGS) AS SUM_WARNINGS FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_account_by_event_name WHERE USER IS NOT NULL AND HOST IS NOT NULL GROUP BY USER, HOST HAVING SUM(SUM_ERRORS) > 0 ORDER BY SUM_ERRORS DESC

queries.description: Shows global wait events sorted by total latency using sys.waits_global_by_latency. Identifies top synchronization and I/O bottlenecks.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary table via sys view; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT events, total_latency, avg_latency, max_latency, total FROM sys.waits_global_by_latency

queries.description: Shows InnoDB purge configuration: threads, batch size, max lag, and max lag delay.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT @@innodb_purge_threads AS purge_threads, @@innodb_purge_batch_size AS purge_batch_size, @@innodb_max_purge_lag AS max_purge_lag, @@innodb_max_purge_lag_delay AS max_purge_lag_delay

queries.description: Shows purge thread count and max purge lag settings with descriptions.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT 'Purge Threads' AS Metric, @@innodb_purge_threads AS Value, 'Number of purge threads' AS Details UNION ALL SELECT 'Max Purge Lag' AS Metric, @@innodb_max_purge_lag AS Value, 'Delay DML if history list exceeds this value' AS Details

queries.description: Finds idle transactions (no active query) older than 5 minutes using I_S.INNODB_TRX. Idle transactions hold locks and prevent purge.

scaling_factor.note: Holds the InnoDB trx_sys mutex while scanning active transactions; scales with active transaction count. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT trx_id, trx_state, trx_started, TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW()) AS age_seconds, trx_mysql_thread_id, trx_tables_locked, trx_rows_locked, trx_rows_modified FROM information_schema.INNODB_TRX WHERE trx_query IS NULL AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW()) > 300 ORDER BY trx_started ASC

queries.description: Finds idle transactions older than 5 minutes using Performance Schema. Safer alternative to I_S.INNODB_TRX.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema transaction events; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT t.EVENT_ID AS trx_id, t.STATE AS trx_state, DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL (t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000) SECOND) AS trx_started, ROUND(t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000, 0) AS age_seconds, th.PROCESSLIST_ID AS trx_mysql_thread_id, t.ISOLATION_LEVEL, t.AUTOCOMMIT, th.PROCESSLIST_USER FROM performance_schema.events_transactions_current t JOIN performance_schema.threads th ON t.THREAD_ID = th.THREAD_ID WHERE t.STATE = 'ACTIVE' AND th.PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL AND th.PROCESSLIST_INFO IS NULL AND ROUND(t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000, 0) > 300 ORDER BY t.TIMER_START

queries.description: Finds active transactions (with running query) older than 60 seconds using I_S.INNODB_TRX.

scaling_factor.note: Holds the InnoDB trx_sys mutex while scanning active transactions; scales with active transaction count. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT trx_id, trx_state, trx_started, TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW()) AS age_seconds, trx_mysql_thread_id, trx_tables_locked, trx_rows_locked, trx_rows_modified, LEFT(trx_query, 100) AS current_query FROM information_schema.INNODB_TRX WHERE trx_query IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, trx_started, NOW()) > 60 ORDER BY trx_started ASC

queries.description: Finds active transactions older than 60 seconds using Performance Schema. Safer alternative.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema transaction events; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT t.EVENT_ID AS trx_id, t.STATE AS trx_state, DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL (t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000) SECOND) AS trx_started, ROUND(t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000, 0) AS age_seconds, th.PROCESSLIST_ID AS trx_mysql_thread_id, t.ISOLATION_LEVEL, t.AUTOCOMMIT, th.PROCESSLIST_USER, LEFT(th.PROCESSLIST_INFO, 100) AS current_query FROM performance_schema.events_transactions_current t JOIN performance_schema.threads th ON t.THREAD_ID = th.THREAD_ID WHERE t.STATE = 'ACTIVE' AND th.PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL AND th.PROCESSLIST_INFO IS NOT NULL AND ROUND(t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000, 0) > 60 ORDER BY t.TIMER_START

queries.description: Summarizes all active transactions: count, oldest age, total locked rows, and modified rows using I_S.INNODB_TRX.

scaling_factor.note: Holds the InnoDB trx_sys mutex while scanning active transactions; scales with active transaction count. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_transactions, TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, MIN(trx_started), NOW()) AS oldest_trx_age_seconds, SUM(trx_rows_locked) AS total_rows_locked, SUM(trx_rows_modified) AS total_modified_rows FROM information_schema.INNODB_TRX

queries.description: Summarizes active transactions using Performance Schema. Safer alternative to I_S.INNODB_TRX.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema transaction events; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_transactions, IFNULL(MAX(ROUND(t.TIMER_WAIT/1000000000000, 0)), 0) AS oldest_trx_age_seconds FROM performance_schema.events_transactions_current t JOIN performance_schema.threads th ON t.THREAD_ID = th.THREAD_ID WHERE t.STATE = 'ACTIVE' AND th.PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL

queries.description: Shows table count, total size, and row count per storage engine. Identifies engine diversity.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); dynamic metadata cached by information_schema_stats_expiry. Scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT ENGINE, COUNT(*) AS table_count, SUM(DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) AS total_size, SUM(TABLE_ROWS) AS total_rows FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') AND TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' GROUP BY ENGINE ORDER BY total_size DESC

queries.description: Shows InnoDB table count and total size per row format (Dynamic, Compressed, Compact, Redundant).

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES data dictionary view (MySQL 8.0+); scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT ROW_FORMAT, COUNT(*) AS table_count, ROUND(SUM(DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) / 1024 / 1024 / 1024, 2) AS total_gb FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') AND ENGINE = 'InnoDB' AND TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' GROUP BY ROW_FORMAT ORDER BY total_gb DESC

queries.description: Finds indexes on Compact/Redundant row format tables where index key length exceeds the 767-byte limit. These can cause issues with large character set columns.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.COLUMNS, I_S.TABLES, I_S.STATISTICS, and I_S.CHARACTER_SETS data dictionary views; scales with table and index count.

queries.command: SELECT DISTINCT a.table_schema, a.table_name, a.index_name, a.INDEX_LEN FROM (SELECT ic.table_schema, ic.table_name, ist.index_name, IF(ist.SUB_PART IS NULL, (ic.CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH * ics.MAXLEN), (ist.SUB_PART * ics.MAXLEN)) AS INDEX_LEN FROM information_schema.columns ic JOIN information_schema.tables it ON it.table_schema = ic.table_schema AND it.table_name = ic.table_name JOIN information_schema.STATISTICS ist ON ist.table_schema = ic.table_schema AND ist.table_name = ic.table_name AND ist.column_name = ic.column_name JOIN information_schema.CHARACTER_SETS ics ON ics.CHARACTER_SET_NAME = ic.CHARACTER_SET_NAME WHERE it.table_schema NOT IN ('information_schema', 'mysql', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND it.row_format IN ('Redundant', 'Compact', 'Compact or Redundant')) AS a WHERE a.INDEX_LEN > 767 ORDER BY a.table_schema, a.table_name, a.index_name

queries.description: Tracks tables with instant DDL column additions and row version counts. High TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS (>50) degrades read performance. MySQL 8.0.29+.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.INNODB_TABLES data dictionary view; scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(NAME, '/', 1) AS schema_name, SUBSTRING_INDEX(NAME, '/', -1) AS table_name, INSTANT_COLS AS instant_cols_pre_8029, TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS, CASE WHEN TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS > 150 THEN 'CRITICAL' WHEN TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS > 50 THEN 'WARNING' ELSE 'OK' END AS status FROM information_schema.INNODB_TABLES WHERE (INSTANT_COLS > 0 OR TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS > 0) AND NAME NOT LIKE 'mysql/%' AND NAME NOT LIKE 'sys/%' ORDER BY TOTAL_ROW_VERSIONS DESC

queries.description: Finds indexes that are redundant (left-prefix of another index) using sys.schema_redundant_indexes. Includes DROP INDEX SQL.

scaling_factor.note: Uses sys.schema_redundant_indexes which reads I_S.STATISTICS; scales with index count.

queries.command: SELECT table_schema, table_name, redundant_index_name, redundant_index_columns, dominant_index_name, dominant_index_columns, sql_drop_index FROM sys.schema_redundant_indexes WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys')

queries.description: Shows per-index I/O statistics: read/insert/update/delete counts and read latency. Identifies hot and cold indexes.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema table_io_waits_summary_by_index_usage table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, IFNULL(INDEX_NAME, 'TABLE_SCAN') AS index_name, COUNT_READ, COUNT_INSERT, COUNT_UPDATE, COUNT_DELETE, COUNT_STAR AS total_operations, ROUND(SUM_TIMER_READ/1000000000000, 2) AS read_latency_sec FROM performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_index_usage WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') AND COUNT_STAR > 0 ORDER BY COUNT_STAR DESC

queries.description: Shows SSL certificate validity dates. Alerts to upcoming certificate expiration.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema global status; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Ssl_server_not_before') AS cert_valid_from, (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Ssl_server_not_after') AS cert_expires

queries.description: Lists users with dangerous privileges: SUPER, GRANT, SHUTDOWN, RELOAD, PROCESS, FILE, CREATE USER.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT user AS User, host AS Host, CONCAT_WS(', ', IF(Super_priv='Y','SUPER',NULL), IF(Grant_priv='Y','GRANT OPTION',NULL), IF(Shutdown_priv='Y','SHUTDOWN',NULL), IF(Reload_priv='Y','RELOAD',NULL), IF(Process_priv='Y','PROCESS',NULL), IF(File_priv='Y','FILE',NULL), IF(Create_user_priv='Y','CREATE USER',NULL)) AS Privileges FROM mysql.user WHERE (Super_priv = 'Y' OR Grant_priv = 'Y' OR Shutdown_priv = 'Y' OR Reload_priv = 'Y' OR Process_priv = 'Y' OR File_priv = 'Y' OR Create_user_priv = 'Y') AND user NOT IN ('mysql.sys', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.infoschema', 'rdsadmin') ORDER BY user

queries.description: Finds accounts using mysql_native_password, which is considered weak compared to caching_sha2_password.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT User, Host, plugin FROM mysql.user WHERE plugin = 'mysql_native_password' AND User NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.sys', 'rdsadmin') ORDER BY User

queries.description: Lists users who can grant privileges to others (GRANT OPTION).

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT DISTINCT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE Grant_priv = 'Y' AND User NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.sys', 'rdsadmin', 'admin') ORDER BY User

queries.description: Finds anonymous accounts (empty username). These are a security risk as any user can connect through them.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT User, Host, IF(authentication_string = '' OR authentication_string IS NULL, 'No Password', 'Has Password') AS password_status FROM mysql.user WHERE User = '' ORDER BY Host

queries.description: Lists users with direct access to system schemas (mysql, performance_schema, sys, information_schema).

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user and mysql.db system privilege tables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT User, Host, Db, Select_priv, Insert_priv, Update_priv, Delete_priv FROM mysql.db WHERE Db IN ('mysql', 'performance_schema', 'sys', 'information_schema') AND User NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.sys', 'rdsadmin') UNION SELECT User, Host, '*' AS Db, Select_priv, Insert_priv, Update_priv, Delete_priv FROM mysql.user WHERE (Select_priv = 'Y' OR Insert_priv = 'Y' OR Update_priv = 'Y' OR Delete_priv = 'Y') AND User NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.sys', 'rdsadmin', 'rdsrepladmin') ORDER BY Db, User

queries.description: Finds accounts with passwords older than 6 months. Helps enforce password rotation policies.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT user, host, password_last_changed, DATEDIFF(NOW(), password_last_changed) AS password_age_days FROM mysql.user WHERE password_last_changed < NOW() - INTERVAL 6 MONTH AND (user, host) NOT IN (('mysql.sys', 'localhost'), ('mysql.session', 'localhost'), ('mysql.infoschema', 'localhost'), ('rdsadmin', 'localhost')) ORDER BY password_last_changed

queries.description: Breaks down connections by processlist state (executing, waiting, etc.) with percentages.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads table; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT IFNULL(PROCESSLIST_STATE, 'NULL') AS state, COUNT(*) AS count, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL), 2) AS pct_of_total FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY PROCESSLIST_STATE ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC

queries.description: Breaks down connections by command type (Query, Sleep, etc.) with percentages.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads table; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT PROCESSLIST_COMMAND AS command, COUNT(*) AS count, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL), 2) AS pct_of_total FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY PROCESSLIST_COMMAND ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC

queries.description: Groups connections into time buckets (< 1 min, 1-5 min, etc.). Identifies long-lived connections.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads table; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT CASE WHEN PROCESSLIST_TIME < 60 THEN '< 1 minute' WHEN PROCESSLIST_TIME < 300 THEN '1-5 minutes' WHEN PROCESSLIST_TIME < 900 THEN '5-15 minutes' WHEN PROCESSLIST_TIME < 3600 THEN '15-60 minutes' WHEN PROCESSLIST_TIME < 14400 THEN '1-4 hours' ELSE '> 4 hours' END AS time_range, COUNT(*) AS count FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY time_range ORDER BY MIN(PROCESSLIST_TIME)

queries.description: Shows client connection attributes: client name, version, OS, and program name per connection.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema session_connect_attrs and threads tables; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT a.PROCESSLIST_ID, CONCAT(t.PROCESSLIST_USER, '@', t.PROCESSLIST_HOST) AS user_host, MAX(IF(a.ATTR_NAME = '_client_name', a.ATTR_VALUE, NULL)) AS client_name, MAX(IF(a.ATTR_NAME = '_client_version', a.ATTR_VALUE, NULL)) AS client_version, MAX(IF(a.ATTR_NAME = '_os', a.ATTR_VALUE, NULL)) AS os, MAX(IF(a.ATTR_NAME = 'program_name', a.ATTR_VALUE, NULL)) AS program_name FROM performance_schema.session_connect_attrs a INNER JOIN performance_schema.threads t ON a.PROCESSLIST_ID = t.PROCESSLIST_ID WHERE t.PROCESSLIST_USER IS NOT NULL GROUP BY a.PROCESSLIST_ID, t.PROCESSLIST_USER, t.PROCESSLIST_HOST

queries.description: Finds connections idle (Sleep) for more than 5 minutes using Performance Schema. Candidates for connection pool tuning.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads table; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT PROCESSLIST_ID, PROCESSLIST_USER, PROCESSLIST_HOST, PROCESSLIST_DB, PROCESSLIST_TIME AS idle_seconds, PROCESSLIST_STATE FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_COMMAND = 'Sleep' AND PROCESSLIST_TIME > 300 AND PROCESSLIST_USER != 'event_scheduler' ORDER BY PROCESSLIST_TIME DESC

queries.description: Finds idle connections using information_schema.processlist. Fallback when PFS is unavailable.

scaling_factor.note: Queries information_schema.processlist which holds the global thread manager mutex; scales with active threads and can cause contention on busy systems. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT ID AS PROCESSLIST_ID, USER AS PROCESSLIST_USER, HOST AS PROCESSLIST_HOST, DB AS PROCESSLIST_DB, TIME AS idle_seconds, STATE AS PROCESSLIST_STATE FROM information_schema.processlist WHERE COMMAND = 'Sleep' AND TIME > 300 AND USER != 'event_scheduler' ORDER BY TIME DESC

queries.description: Finds non-idle connections active for more than 60 seconds using Performance Schema.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads table; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT PROCESSLIST_ID, PROCESSLIST_USER, PROCESSLIST_HOST, PROCESSLIST_DB, PROCESSLIST_COMMAND, PROCESSLIST_TIME AS active_seconds, PROCESSLIST_STATE, LEFT(PROCESSLIST_INFO, 100) AS query_snippet FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE PROCESSLIST_COMMAND != 'Sleep' AND PROCESSLIST_COMMAND IS NOT NULL AND PROCESSLIST_TIME > 60 ORDER BY PROCESSLIST_TIME DESC

queries.description: Shows all current InnoDB data locks on user schemas. Pre-8.0.40: holds global trx_sys mutex while scanning ALL active transactions/locks, which can cause complete InnoDB stalls on busy systems. 8.0.40+: redesigned with bucket-based iteration, much safer.

scaling_factor.note: Pre-8.0.40: holds global InnoDB trx_sys mutex during scan with can stall InnoDB on busy systems with many locks. 8.0.40+: uses bucket-based iteration without exclusive global mutex. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID, THREAD_ID, OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, INDEX_NAME, LOCK_TYPE, LOCK_MODE, LOCK_STATUS, LOCK_DATA FROM performance_schema.data_locks WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys')

queries.description: Shows current lock wait relationships: which transaction is waiting for which blocker. Pre-8.0.40: same global mutex risk as data_locks. 8.0.40+: redesigned, much safer.

scaling_factor.note: Pre-8.0.40: holds global InnoDB trx_sys mutex during scan which can stall InnoDB on busy systems with many locks. 8.0.40+: uses bucket-based iteration without exclusive global mutex. Gated behind requires_extended_checks.

queries.command: SELECT REQUESTING_ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID AS waiting_trx, BLOCKING_ENGINE_TRANSACTION_ID AS blocking_trx, REQUESTING_THREAD_ID AS waiting_thread, BLOCKING_THREAD_ID AS blocking_thread FROM performance_schema.data_lock_waits

queries.description: Shows lock-related configuration: lock wait timeout, metadata lock timeout, deadlock detection, and deadlock logging.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT 'innodb_lock_wait_timeout' AS Parameter, @@innodb_lock_wait_timeout AS Value, 'Seconds a transaction waits for a row lock before giving up' AS Details UNION ALL SELECT 'lock_wait_timeout', @@lock_wait_timeout, 'Seconds to wait for metadata locks' UNION ALL SELECT 'innodb_deadlock_detect', @@innodb_deadlock_detect, 'Enables automatic deadlock detection (ON recommended)' UNION ALL SELECT 'innodb_print_all_deadlocks', @@innodb_print_all_deadlocks, 'Logs all deadlocks to error log for debugging'

queries.description: Shows InnoDB row lock statistics: total waits, wait time, average wait, current waits, and deadlock count.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server status counters via Performance Schema; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT 'Innodb_row_lock_waits' AS Variable_name, VARIABLE_VALUE AS Value, 'Total number of times InnoDB had to wait for a row lock' AS Details FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_row_lock_waits' UNION ALL SELECT 'Innodb_row_lock_time', VARIABLE_VALUE, 'Total time spent waiting for row locks (milliseconds)' FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_row_lock_time' UNION ALL SELECT 'Innodb_row_lock_time_avg', VARIABLE_VALUE, 'Average time to acquire a row lock (milliseconds)' FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_row_lock_time_avg' UNION ALL SELECT 'Innodb_row_lock_current_waits', VARIABLE_VALUE, 'Number of row locks currently being waited for' FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_row_lock_current_waits' UNION ALL SELECT 'Innodb_deadlocks', VARIABLE_VALUE, 'Total number of deadlocks detected since server start' FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_deadlocks'

queries.description: Shows P95 query latency per digest with P95/avg ratio. Identifies queries with tail latency issues. MySQL/Aurora only.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT SCHEMA_NAME, LEFT(DIGEST_TEXT, 80) AS query_digest, COUNT_STAR AS exec_count, ROUND(AVG_TIMER_WAIT/1000000, 2) AS avg_ms, ROUND(QUANTILE_95/1000000, 2) AS p95_ms, ROUND(QUANTILE_95/NULLIF(AVG_TIMER_WAIT, 0), 2) AS p95_avg_ratio, ROUND(MAX_TIMER_WAIT/1000000, 2) AS max_ms FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE SCHEMA_NAME NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') AND COUNT_STAR > 10 ORDER BY QUANTILE_95 DESC

queries.description: Shows P99 query latency per digest with P99/avg ratio. Identifies extreme tail latency outliers. MySQL/Aurora only.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT SCHEMA_NAME, LEFT(DIGEST_TEXT, 80) AS query_digest, COUNT_STAR AS exec_count, ROUND(AVG_TIMER_WAIT/1000000, 2) AS avg_ms, ROUND(QUANTILE_99/1000000, 2) AS p99_ms, ROUND(QUANTILE_99/NULLIF(AVG_TIMER_WAIT, 0), 2) AS p99_avg_ratio, ROUND(MAX_TIMER_WAIT/1000000, 2) AS max_ms FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE SCHEMA_NAME NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') AND COUNT_STAR > 10 ORDER BY QUANTILE_99 DESC

queries.description: Finds query digests that have produced errors or warnings. Helps identify problematic SQL patterns.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema events_statements_summary_by_digest table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT SCHEMA_NAME, LEFT(DIGEST_TEXT, 100) AS query_digest, COUNT_STAR AS exec_count, SUM_ERRORS, SUM_WARNINGS FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest WHERE (SUM_ERRORS > 0 OR SUM_WARNINGS > 0) AND SCHEMA_NAME NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') ORDER BY SUM_ERRORS DESC, SUM_WARNINGS DESC

queries.description: Comprehensive statement analysis via sys.statement_analysis: execution count, latency, rows examined, and temp tables.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary table via sys view; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT db, LEFT(query, 60) AS query_snippet, exec_count, total_latency, avg_latency, max_latency, rows_examined_avg, tmp_tables FROM sys.statement_analysis WHERE db NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys')

queries.description: Finds statements performing full table scans via sys.statements_with_full_table_scans.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary table via sys view; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT db, LEFT(query, 60) AS query_snippet, exec_count, total_latency, no_index_used_count, rows_sent_avg, rows_examined_avg FROM sys.statements_with_full_table_scans WHERE db NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys')

queries.description: Finds tables being full-scanned with row counts and latency via sys.schema_tables_with_full_table_scans.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary table via sys view; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT object_schema, object_name, rows_full_scanned, latency FROM sys.schema_tables_with_full_table_scans WHERE object_schema NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys')

queries.description: Finds statements performing sorts with merge pass counts via sys.statements_with_sorting.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary table via sys view; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT db, LEFT(query, 60) AS query_snippet, exec_count, total_latency, sort_merge_passes, avg_sort_merges, rows_sorted FROM sys.statements_with_sorting WHERE db NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys')

queries.description: Finds statements creating temporary tables (memory and disk) via sys.statements_with_temp_tables.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary table via sys view; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT db, LEFT(query, 60) AS query_snippet, exec_count, total_latency, memory_tmp_tables, disk_tmp_tables FROM sys.statements_with_temp_tables WHERE db NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys')

queries.description: Finds accounts that disconnect without sending COM_QUIT. May indicate connection pool misconfiguration or application bugs.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema summary tables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT ess.user, ess.host, a.total_connections, (a.total_connections - a.current_connections) - ess.count_star AS not_closed, ROUND(((a.total_connections - a.current_connections) - ess.count_star) * 100 / NULLIF((a.total_connections - a.current_connections), 0), 2) AS pct_not_closed FROM performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_account_by_event_name ess JOIN performance_schema.accounts a ON (ess.user = a.user AND ess.host = a.host) WHERE ess.event_name = 'statement/com/Quit' AND (a.total_connections - a.current_connections) > ess.count_star ORDER BY not_closed DESC

queries.description: Finds active (non-locked, non-expired) accounts that have never connected since server restart. MySQL/Aurora variant.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table and Performance Schema users table; negligible overhead.

queries.name: Accounts Never Connected Since Restart
queries.command: SELECT DISTINCT mu.user AS USER, mu.host AS HOST FROM mysql.user mu LEFT JOIN performance_schema.users psu ON mu.user = psu.user WHERE psu.user IS NULL AND mu.user NOT IN ('mysql.infoschema', 'mysql.session', 'mysql.sys') AND (mu.authentication_string != '' AND mu.password_expired = 'N' AND mu.account_locked = 'N') ORDER BY mu.user

queries.description: Finds active accounts that have never connected since restart. MariaDB variant using mysql.global_priv for lock status.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user, mysql.global_priv, and Performance Schema users table; negligible overhead.

queries.name: Accounts Never Connected Since Restart
queries.command: SELECT DISTINCT mu.user AS USER, mu.host AS HOST FROM mysql.user mu JOIN mysql.global_priv gp ON mu.User = gp.User AND mu.Host = gp.Host LEFT JOIN performance_schema.users psu ON mu.user = psu.user WHERE psu.user IS NULL AND mu.user NOT IN ('mariadb.sys') AND mu.authentication_string != '' AND mu.password_expired = 'N' AND COALESCE(JSON_VALUE(gp.Priv, '$.account_locked'), 'false') != 'true' ORDER BY mu.user

queries.description: Shows custom, RDS, and Aurora-specific server variables.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE variable_name LIKE 'custom_%' OR variable_name LIKE 'rds_%' OR variable_name LIKE 'aurora_%'

queries.description: Shows replication filter rules per channel. Identifies which databases/tables are being filtered during replication.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema replication_applier_filters table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT CHANNEL_NAME, FILTER_NAME, FILTER_RULE, CONFIGURED_BY, COUNTER FROM performance_schema.replication_applier_filters ORDER BY CHANNEL_NAME, FILTER_NAME

queries.description: Counts total, SSL, and non-SSL connections. Shows what percentage of connections are encrypted.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads and status_by_thread tables; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.threads WHERE TYPE='FOREGROUND' AND PROCESSLIST_COMMAND != 'Daemon') AS total_connections, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.threads t JOIN performance_schema.status_by_thread s ON t.THREAD_ID = s.THREAD_ID WHERE t.TYPE='FOREGROUND' AND t.PROCESSLIST_COMMAND != 'Daemon' AND s.VARIABLE_NAME = 'Ssl_cipher' AND s.VARIABLE_VALUE != '') AS ssl_connections, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM performance_schema.threads t JOIN performance_schema.status_by_thread s ON t.THREAD_ID = s.THREAD_ID WHERE t.TYPE='FOREGROUND' AND t.PROCESSLIST_COMMAND != 'Daemon' AND s.VARIABLE_NAME = 'Ssl_cipher' AND (s.VARIABLE_VALUE = '' OR s.VARIABLE_VALUE IS NULL)) AS non_ssl_connections

queries.description: Shows SSL/TLS version used by each connected thread. Identifies clients using outdated TLS versions.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Performance Schema threads and status_by_thread tables; scales with thread count but negligible overhead with no global mutex.

queries.command: SELECT t.THREAD_ID, t.PROCESSLIST_USER AS user, t.PROCESSLIST_HOST AS host, t.CONNECTION_TYPE, s.VARIABLE_VALUE AS ssl_version FROM performance_schema.threads t LEFT JOIN performance_schema.status_by_thread s ON t.THREAD_ID = s.THREAD_ID AND s.VARIABLE_NAME = 'Ssl_version' WHERE t.CONNECTION_TYPE IS NOT NULL AND t.PROCESSLIST_USER IS NOT NULL ORDER BY t.THREAD_ID

queries.description: Shows I/O statistics aggregated by event type (redo log, data files, temp files, etc.). Identifies which I/O subsystems are busiest.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema file_summary_by_event_name table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT EVENT_NAME, COUNT_STAR AS TOTAL_OPERATIONS, SUM_NUMBER_OF_BYTES_READ AS BYTES_READ, SUM_NUMBER_OF_BYTES_WRITE AS BYTES_WRITTEN, ROUND(SUM_TIMER_WAIT/1000000000, 4) AS TOTAL_LATENCY_MS FROM performance_schema.file_summary_by_event_name WHERE COUNT_STAR > 0 ORDER BY SUM_TIMER_WAIT DESC

queries.description: Shows per-index I/O operation counts and read latency. Identifies hot indexes driving the most I/O.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema table_io_waits_summary_by_index_usage table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA AS 'Schema', OBJECT_NAME AS 'Table', INDEX_NAME AS 'Index Name', COUNT_READ AS 'Read Count', COUNT_INSERT AS 'Insert Count', COUNT_UPDATE AS 'Update Count', COUNT_DELETE AS 'Delete Count', (COUNT_READ + COUNT_INSERT + COUNT_UPDATE + COUNT_DELETE) AS 'Total Operations', ROUND(SUM_TIMER_READ / 1000000000, 2) AS 'Read Latency (ms)' FROM performance_schema.table_io_waits_summary_by_index_usage WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'performance_schema', 'information_schema', 'sys') AND INDEX_NAME IS NOT NULL AND (COUNT_READ + COUNT_INSERT + COUNT_UPDATE + COUNT_DELETE) > 0 ORDER BY (COUNT_READ + COUNT_INSERT + COUNT_UPDATE + COUNT_DELETE) DESC

queries.description: Calculates redo log usage percentage. High usage indicates checkpoint lag or insufficient redo log capacity. MySQL-only.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server status counters and variables via Performance Schema; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT ROUND((current_lsn - checkpoint_lsn) / (1024 * 1024), 2) AS redo_log_mb_used, ROUND(((current_lsn - checkpoint_lsn) / (@@innodb_redo_log_capacity)) * 100, 2) AS redo_log_pct_used FROM (SELECT (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_redo_log_current_lsn') AS current_lsn, (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_redo_log_checkpoint_lsn') AS checkpoint_lsn) AS lsn_values

queries.description: Counts tables without a primary key. Used as a health check metric.

scaling_factor.note: Reads I_S.TABLES and I_S.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE data dictionary views (MySQL 8.0+); scales with table count.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS tables_without_pk FROM information_schema.TABLES t LEFT JOIN information_schema.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE k ON t.TABLE_SCHEMA = k.TABLE_SCHEMA AND t.TABLE_NAME = k.TABLE_NAME AND k.CONSTRAINT_NAME = 'PRIMARY' WHERE t.TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'mysql', 'sys') AND t.TABLE_TYPE = 'BASE TABLE' AND k.CONSTRAINT_NAME IS NULL

queries.description: Counts accounts with empty passwords. Used as a health check metric.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS empty_password_count FROM mysql.user WHERE authentication_string = '' AND plugin NOT IN ('auth_socket', 'unix_socket') AND NOT (account_locked = 'Y' AND password_expired = 'Y')

queries.description: Calculates connection usage as a percentage of max_connections. High values indicate connection exhaustion risk.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server status counters and variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT ROUND((VARIABLE_VALUE / @@max_connections * 100), 2) AS connection_usage_pct FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Threads_connected'

queries.description: Calculates InnoDB buffer pool hit rate. Values below 99% may indicate the buffer pool is too small.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server status counters via Performance Schema; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT ROUND(100 - ((CAST(bp_reads AS DECIMAL(20,2)) / NULLIF(CAST(bp_read_requests AS DECIMAL(20,2)), 0)) * 100), 2) AS buffer_pool_hit_rate FROM (SELECT (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_buffer_pool_reads') AS bp_reads, (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Innodb_buffer_pool_read_requests') AS bp_read_requests) AS bp_stats

queries.description: Counts AUTO_INCREMENT columns that have consumed more than 90% of their data type range. Exhaustion makes further INSERTs fail with duplicate key errors.

scaling_factor.note: Reads sys.schema_auto_increment_columns, which aggregates over information_schema; cost grows with table count.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS auto_increment_critical_count FROM sys.schema_auto_increment_columns WHERE auto_increment_ratio > 0.9

queries.description: Counts replication applier workers currently reporting an error. The HAVING clause returns no rows at all when the instance is not a replica, so the health check is skipped rather than reporting OK on a source.

scaling_factor.note: Reads a small Performance Schema table with one row per applier worker.

queries.command: SELECT COUNT(*) AS replication_error_count FROM performance_schema.replication_applier_status_by_worker WHERE LAST_ERROR_NUMBER <> 0 HAVING (SELECT COUNT(1) FROM performance_schema.replication_connection_status) > 0

queries.description: Lists accounts that are currently locked (account_locked = Y).

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT user, host, account_locked FROM mysql.user WHERE account_locked = 'Y' ORDER BY user, host

queries.description: Shows the count of connection attempts to locked accounts since server start.

scaling_factor.note: Reads a server status counter; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'Locked_connects'

queries.description: Lists accounts with expired passwords.

scaling_factor.note: Reads mysql.user system privilege table; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT user, host, password_expired, password_last_changed FROM mysql.user WHERE password_expired = 'Y' ORDER BY user, host

queries.description: Reads key configuration variables that may trigger warnings: sync_binlog, flush settings, binlog format, storage engine defaults.

scaling_factor.note: Reads server variables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT @@sync_binlog AS sync_binlog, @@innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit AS innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit, @@foreign_key_checks AS foreign_key_checks, @@innodb_stats_persistent AS innodb_stats_persistent, @@innodb_stats_auto_recalc AS innodb_stats_auto_recalc, @@binlog_row_image AS binlog_row_image, @@binlog_format AS binlog_format, @@default_storage_engine AS default_storage_engine, @@log_output AS log_output, @@max_connect_errors AS max_connect_errors, @@log_bin AS log_bin, @@general_log AS general_log, @@slow_query_log AS slow_query_log

queries.description: Shows transaction distribution across parallel replication workers. Uneven distribution indicates suboptimal parallelism.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema replication and transaction summary tables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT rw.CHANNEL_NAME, rw.THREAD_ID AS replica_worker_thread_id, ts.COUNT_STAR AS number_of_trx_executed, ROUND(ts.COUNT_STAR / SUM(ts.COUNT_STAR) OVER (PARTITION BY rw.CHANNEL_NAME) * 100, 2) AS percent_of_trx_executed_by_worker FROM performance_schema.replication_applier_status_by_worker AS rw JOIN performance_schema.events_transactions_summary_by_thread_by_event_name AS ts ON rw.THREAD_ID = ts.THREAD_ID WHERE ts.EVENT_NAME = 'transaction' AND (SELECT COUNT(1) FROM performance_schema.replication_connection_status) > 0

queries.description: Shows the last 10 SQL statements executed by each long-running transaction (>5 min). Helps diagnose what the transaction has been doing.

scaling_factor.note: Reads pre-aggregated Performance Schema transaction, statement history, and threads tables; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT mysql_pid, trx_duration, trx_state, sql_text, stmt_execution_time, rows_sent, rows_modified, rows_examined, tmp_disk_tables, error_info FROM (SELECT thr.PROCESSLIST_ID AS mysql_pid, FORMAT_PICO_TIME(trx.TIMER_WAIT) AS trx_duration, trx.STATE AS trx_state, stm.SQL_TEXT AS sql_text, FORMAT_PICO_TIME(stm.TIMER_WAIT) AS stmt_execution_time, stm.ROWS_SENT AS rows_sent, stm.ROWS_AFFECTED AS rows_modified, stm.ROWS_EXAMINED AS rows_examined, stm.CREATED_TMP_DISK_TABLES AS tmp_disk_tables, CASE WHEN stm.ERRORS > 0 THEN CONCAT('Error: ', stm.MESSAGE_TEXT) ELSE 'OK' END AS error_info, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY stm.THREAD_ID ORDER BY stm.EVENT_ID DESC) as row_num FROM performance_schema.events_transactions_current trx JOIN performance_schema.threads thr ON trx.THREAD_ID = thr.THREAD_ID JOIN performance_schema.events_statements_history stm ON stm.THREAD_ID = trx.THREAD_ID WHERE trx.STATE = 'ACTIVE' AND trx.TIMER_WAIT > (300 * 1000000000000) AND thr.PROCESSLIST_ID IS NOT NULL) AS long_trx_diagnostics WHERE row_num <= 10 ORDER BY mysql_pid, row_num ASC

queries.description: Shows Aurora in-memory relay log status, fallback counts, and recovery counts. In-memory relay log improves replica performance.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Aurora-specific Performance Schema status counters; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, VARIABLE_VALUE, CASE VARIABLE_NAME WHEN 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_status' THEN 'In-memory relay log status. ENABLED = optimal replica performance' WHEN 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_disabled_reason' THEN 'Reason why in-memory relay log is disabled (if applicable)' WHEN 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_fallback_count' THEN 'Times relay log fell back to persistent storage (large transactions)' WHEN 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_recovery_count' THEN 'Times relay log recovered from fallback state' END AS Details FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME IN ('Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_status', 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_disabled_reason', 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_fallback_count', 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_recovery_count') ORDER BY FIELD(VARIABLE_NAME, 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_status', 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_disabled_reason', 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_fallback_count', 'Aurora_in_memory_relaylog_recovery_count')

queries.description: Shows total replication bytes received by this Aurora instance.

scaling_factor.note: Reads Aurora-specific Performance Schema status counters; negligible overhead.

queries.command: SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, VARIABLE_VALUE, CASE VARIABLE_NAME WHEN 'Aurora_repl_bytes_received' THEN 'Total bytes received from replication source since instance start' END AS Details FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME = 'Aurora_repl_bytes_received'
